newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aluminum shipments fall 3.7 pct in Jan to Sep.
newsitem.headline: U.S. aluminum shipments fall 3.7 pct in Jan to Sep.

text.p: U.S. aluminum shipments fell 3.7 percent in the first nine months of the year compared to the same period last year, but new orders in October rebounded, the Aluminum Association reported.
Preliminary figures for September indicate that industry shipments, including exports, totaled 1.696 billion pounds, a dip of 4.4 percent from September 1995.
Compared to August, shipments in September were down 8.3 percent. In January through September shipments totaled 15.652 billion pounds.

U.S. exports of aluminum ingot and mill products were reported at 233 million pounds in September, down 1.9 percent from September 1995. Imports in September were 424 million pounds, up 12.1 percent over the same month in 1995.
Estimated net new industry orders of aluminum mill products, totaling 1.371 billion pounds in October, jumped 17.8 percent from the October 1995 level.

New orders in October for domestic can stock totaling 392 million pounds, were up 34.9 percent over October 1995, while orders for other sheet and plate, including exports, rose 14.4 percent to 466 million pounds.
October orders overall rose 10.5 percent over September.
U.S producer inventories in September fell 39 million pounds from August to 4.18 billion pounds.
Scrap consumption rose 5.7 percent in the first nine months of the year to 6.298 billion pounds.
